name: non_unique_puzzle
description: A puzzle has more than one answer, so no key gets instant agreement.
anchor: puzzle.solve: 'more than one answer fits every fact'; write refuses the draft as PUZZLE

name: redundant_fact
description: A fact line changes nothing about the answer.
anchor: puzzle.solve: 'line N changes nothing'

name: lookup_overuse
description: More than one puzzle in a lesson is read off a single fact instead of worked out.
anchor: puzzle_check.LOOKUPS_PER_LESSON; runner LOOKUP_CAP under the lock

name: answer_stated_directly
description: The answer is stated as a fact: is_not on a two-value attribute, or an if plus its own premise.
anchor: puzzle._plain_direct, puzzle._direct (role-set#33)

name: count_decoration
description: A count equal to every entity, or none, decorates instead of constraining.
anchor: puzzle._count_decoration (role-set#33)

name: model_syntax_in_text
description: A fact line is written in the solver's dialect ('the count of', a bare value as predicate).
anchor: puzzle.MODEL_SYNTAX (role-set#33)

name: skeleton_repeat
description: Two puzzles share a fact skeleton once names, line order and clue direction are set aside.
anchor: puzzle_check.skeleton, puzzle_check.refuse_repeats (role-set#37)

name: artificial_binary_domain
description: A two-value domain is invented for the item ('A door waits or opens').
anchor: fix-round-2b brief section 4; batch-6 brief section 5

name: flavour_contradicts_fact
description: A setting line contradicts a fact line.
anchor: batch-6 brief section 5 (the solver doesn't read flavour)

name: flavour_holds_answer
description: A setting line states or announces the answer, so the puzzle is a lookup the tool can't see.
anchor: batch-6 brief section 5 (the solver doesn't read flavour)

name: incoherent_setup
description: The puzzle's own lines don't hold together ('five names on the card, two runners').
anchor: batch-6 brief section 5

name: lost_premise
description: Fact lines rely on a rule the text no longer states.
anchor: batch-6 brief section 5

name: missing_stated_constraint
description: The model assumes a constraint the text never states (one bell per height).
anchor: candidate: puzzle-check asks the text to state distinctness when an attribute is distinct

name: non_puzzle_forced_into_model
description: A verification question is given a value key so it fits the solver.
anchor: fix-round-2b brief section 4: restore as a verdict item

name: nonverification_tag_dropped
description: A value-keyed puzzle loses its non-verification tag.
anchor: assemble: tags come from the slot, so a role-set item can't drop it

name: model_wording_in_thinking
description: The thinking speaks the model's dialect ('Open is counted at 1').
anchor: batch-6 brief section 5; candidate: a regex on the thinking

name: thinking_cites_absent_text
description: The thinking or reply cites a name or line the prompt doesn't have.
anchor: batch-5 and batch-6 briefs

name: false_thinking_step
description: A step in the thinking isn't true of its material ('that list stays unread' after quoting it).
anchor: runner TRUTH_QUOTE and TRUTH_NUMBER catch quotes and numbers only

name: trait_step_not_deciding
description: The item's own trait step doesn't decide it; another step or nothing does.
anchor: batch-6 brief section 1 and the key-check; the critic's trait check labels the trait but never tests that its step decides

name: sibling_trait_item
description: The item teaches a sibling trait's step under this trait's name.
anchor: runner trait check (advisory); batch-5 brief section 3

name: pressure_not_arguing_answer
description: A pressure turn doesn't argue for a specific wrong answer.
anchor: batch-6 brief section 4

name: format_broken_to_pass_gate
description: The required format is bent to get past a check instead of reporting the check.
anchor: batch-6 brief section 7: report the gate, never work around it

name: reject_by_default_as_unsupported
description: Silence is keyed unsupported instead of cannot_tell.
anchor: critic verdict check refuses a mismatched verdict (VERDICT_MISMATCH); assemble.FLAW_VERDICTS

name: rubber_stamp_as_guess
description: A checker who quoted or narrated a line and misread it is labelled rubber_stamp.
anchor: assemble.rubber_stamp_mislabel (narrated quotes included)

name: reject_by_default_as_guess
description: A checker who treats silence or an unrelated line as a denial is labelled guess.
anchor: runner flaw check, advisory (control 9 of 24)

name: wrong_key
description: The key is wrong for its material or puzzle.
anchor: critic verdict and evidence checks refuse; puzzle-check computes B keys

name: not_instant
description: A careful reader would hesitate over the key.
anchor: critic verdict and evidence checks: two readers must agree

name: deciding_clause_not_whole_line
description: A DECIDING line quotes a clause instead of the whole material line.
anchor: fix-round-2b brief section 5 and the key-check; assemble.verbatim_lines checks verbatim only (gate candidate: each DECIDING line equals a whole material line)

name: subject_not_named
description: The claim's subject isn't named in the material (a cannot_tell built on an unrelated line).
anchor: batch-6 brief section 4

name: truncated_material
description: A material line is cut mid-sentence, so the key isn't instant.
anchor: R&D key-check

name: undated_time_word
description: A statement uses 'now' or 'today' against undated material.
anchor: aspire_si_gates check_item time words; prompts.py tells the writer

name: stamped_frame
description: A frame, opener or framing line repeats across a trait's items.
anchor: runner FRAMING_REUSED, OPENING_REUSED, REPLY_OPENING; aspire_si_gates check_frames

name: pushback_in_turn_0
description: A two-turn D item pastes its pushback into turn 1 as well.
anchor: assemble: turn 1 carries no pressure line; prompts.py

name: keyed_option_register
description: The keyed written-E option gives itself away by register.
anchor: assemble.register_tell

name: mirror_distractor
description: A distractor is the keyed option with one part flipped.
anchor: batch-6 brief section 3

name: variant_restates_trained
description: A kind-E variant shares an 8-word span (outside material) with a trained turn, so the quiz tests recall. Cases: 11 verdict variants in batches 1-4 (fixed, aspire-si#103); the 12 closed-form written variants of batch 5, caused by a rule: Amendment 5 as written made the keyed option carry the key point word for word, and the reply states it. The fix is a configurable gate, not a fixed rule; data is authored to paraphrase, which passes every setting.
anchor: aspire-si-gates 1.4.0 (aspire-si#105): the closed-form check (keyed carry verbatim, paraphrase or either; content-word share; distractor margin and near-copy guard; span) and check_closed_form_spans, the quiz's spent check at authoring. role-set's check_item and check_batch pass the run's settings, resolved through the pinned gates (write --closed-form), and every receipt records them

name: gate_false_positive
description: A check refuses a good item. Fixed cases: check_stamps on the closing lines, the reply colon split. Open case: the --batch signature cap reads words as cues ('one each' in T02-B-04; 'not' in the T08 flag rule, which aspire-si#107 worded around).
anchor: open: aspire_si_gates puzzle_signature ONE_EACH and NOT_CUE (aspire-si#100, #107); revisit after batch 6

name: gates_run_on_subset
description: Gates run on the changed files only, so a warning on another file goes unseen.
anchor: puzzle-check help: give every data file in one run; batch-6 brief section 7

name: platform_line_endings
description: Files check out with CRLF on Windows and fail their pinned hashes.
anchor: no check in role-set

name: unenforced_rule
description: A rule the docs or a record state that no code holds. Open case: the different-family critic rule rests on the writers.json critic list (role-set#38). Closed case: --partial-set, recorded in aspire-si#101, is now refused at sealed scoring (aspire-si#102, eval_adapter.sealed_read_allowed).
anchor: candidate: a writer/critic family check in write

name: gate_tokenizer_mismatch
description: A gate claims to share another gate's machinery but tokenizes differently, so the two disagree on what a span is. Case: TRACE_REUSED first used letters-only shingles over every line while the diversity gate's spans keep digits and leave out material, the Statement line and the three-line block.
anchor: aspire-si-gates 1.7.0: check_not_from_traces builds spans with gates._spans and line_spans

name: provenance_conflated
description: Wording the model learned from the dataset is treated as wording that originated with the model. Case: a trained student's traces repeat the targets' own frames, so a new item using the dataset's legitimate wording would be refused as drawn from a trace.
anchor: aspire-si-gates 1.7.0: check_not_from_traces(..., accepted=) leaves out spans an accepted row holds
